PullRequest.Title: sessions: Fix cloud session rename via Mission Control
PullRequest.Body:

Disconnected cloud sandbox sessions expose Rename, but the inherited AHP-only implementation silently does nothing without a live connection.

Rename the owning Mission Control task using `PATCH /agents/tasks/{task_id}`, update the local title after success, and use the existing AHP rename once when already connected. Update the existing discovery inventory/cache and route default-chat rename through the same operation. Sessions not owned by the discovered task continue to use AHP.

Deliberately does not add pending-command storage, reconnect replay, or title reconciliation. The Tasks API updates the task record, not the host title, so a later connection after an offline rename can report the old host title. Host-reported titles remain authoritative.

No linked issue; reported during this session.

### Validation

- `npm run compile-client` — passed, zero compilation errors.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/remoteAgentHost/cloudSandboxApiService.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/remoteAgentHost/test/browser/cloudSandboxAgentHostContribution.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/remoteAgentHost/test/browser/remoteAgentHostSessionsProvider.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost/test/browser/localAgentHostSessionsProvider.test.ts --grep "CloudSandbox|RemoteAgentHostSessionsProvider.*(rename|title)|LocalAgentHostSessionsProvider.*(rename|[Tt]itle)"` — passed, 227 tests.
- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed.
- `npm run valid-layers-check` — passed.
- ESLint on changed TypeScript files and commit hygiene hook — passed.

Live Mission Control/UI validation was not performed. Manually rename a disconnected discovered sandbox session and verify its task name/local title update without connecting; rename an already-connected session and verify the host title updates too.

(Written by Copilot)

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed trigger, restored-row overlap, request limits/concurrency, and late generation check are all explicit in the code and the new in-flight test. Exact user inventory size and request duration vary, which limits severity but not the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Mission Control listTasks/getTask network requests and their response parsing
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The wasted work grows with the cold full-discovery inventory: two repository scopes, up to 10 pages of 100 summaries each, followed by one getTask request per uncached sandbox task at concurrency 5.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Excessive network I/O and lower discovery throughput, with avoidable API/rate-limit pressure while the invalidated scan remains in flight.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Renaming a restored disconnected sandbox was a no-op, and a connected rename only dispatched to AHP; neither operation invalidated Mission Control discovery or caused its remaining requests to be discarded.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: After the new PATCH succeeds, this line increments the discovery generation. listSessions checks that generation only after all list pages and all limiter-queued getTask calls have completed, so an overlapping scan continues doing work even though it must return a failed invalidation result.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added `this._discoveryGeneration++;` at line 546 creates a new invalidation trigger for session rename. Unlike the pre-PR rename path, this trigger can fire from a restored offline row while cold discovery is still fetching tasks.
Findings.Title: Stop invalidated discovery before issuing the remaining requests
Findings.Impact: A realistic cold-start overlap exists because persisted rows are restored before network discovery finishes: renaming one of those rows can leave the startup scan issuing getTask calls for every remaining sandbox task (and any remaining pages), all of which are thrown away. This increases Mission Control traffic and can delay later refreshes behind the still-running scan.
Findings.Evidence: CloudSandboxSessionContribution restores and seeds persisted sessions before awaiting listSessions. listSessions captures _discoveryGeneration at line 287, can scan up to 2×10 pages, then queues getTask for sandboxTasks with a limiter of 5; it does not compare the generation again until line 438 after Promise.all. The added rename path increments the generation at line 546, and the added test "invalidates discovery in flight when a task is renamed" proves this can occur while getTask is pending and that the completed scan is discarded.
Findings.Recommendation: Preserve stale-response protection while stopping fan-out: cancel the active discovery with a per-pass CancellationTokenSource when rename commits, or check the captured generation before each page and before each limiter-queued getTask so no further boundary calls are issued after invalidation. Keep the next pass's `needsRefresh` behavior for the renamed task.

Scenarios.Scenario: Rename a restored/disconnected cloud sandbox session, including its default chat
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Resolve the GitHub session, complete one Mission Control PATCH (10 s timeout), update the in-memory environment and persisted inventory, then publish the local session-title change. All of this is on the rename completion path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one PATCH per committed rename; no batching or retry loop in this path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A disconnected rename returned without any boundary call.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The PATCH must complete before the local title and persisted inventory are updated.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist the renamed per-session discovery inventory entry through IStorageService.storeAll
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One changed storage entry for the renamed session after an O(number of discovered environments) in-memory comparison.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A disconnected rename did not persist anything.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs synchronously after PATCH success and before the provider publishes the local title.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected session per rename; inventory persistence scans all discovered environments in memory but writes only changed entries. A normal commit issues one task PATCH.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No rename coalescer or limiter, but the ordinary UI commits one title at a time. The PATCH is awaited serially before inventory/local-title updates.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A restored inventory makes the row available before cold discovery. The discovered-task positive cache is updated optimistically, then marked needsRefresh so the next incremental scan performs one authoritative getTask even if the list omits the task; authentication-session lookup follows the existing service behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the one PATCH and inventory write path; both are directly traced from the added override and tests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical inventory size and profile-storage backend latency are not measured, but ordinary rename cardinality is one.
Scenarios.Verdict: The single PATCH and one changed inventory write are necessary, bounded costs for offline rename and are not independently reportable. The overlap with cold discovery is covered separately.

Scenarios.Scenario: Rename the discovered session while its cloud sandbox is connected
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The new Mission Control PATCH completes first; only then does the inherited provider update the local title and dispatch SessionTitleChanged to the connected host.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: PATCH the owning Mission Control task
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Connected rename immediately updated local state and dispatched to AHP without a Mission Control request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Newly precedes local title publication and host dispatch, with a 10 s request timeout.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch SessionTitleChanged on the connected AHP session channel
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same single dispatch occurred immediately; the diff changes its ordering behind PATCH.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Occurs only after the new PATCH succeeds.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One task and one host session per user rename.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The PATCH and AHP dispatch are deliberately serialized; there is no fan-out. The host dispatch itself is synchronous from this call path.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The task cache is updated and marked needsRefresh exactly as for offline rename; the connected host remains authoritative when it later reports a title.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that the network request is newly serialized ahead of the existing dispatch.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Mission Control latency distribution is unknown; the timeout is 10 s, but rename is a low-frequency explicit action.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding: the added one-request latency is the core cross-client persistence operation and the ordering enforces the PR's success semantics; there is no scaling or repeated-work mechanism with a bounded behavior-preserving alternative.

Scenarios.Scenario: Rename a restored row while cold Mission Control discovery is in flight
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Rename itself completes after its PATCH, but startup discovery is an important background path: listSessions scans task pages and limiter-queues getTask calls. The rename generation bump guarantees the scan will be discarded, yet the scan checks generation only after all queued requests complete.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: List Mission Control task pages for repository and workspace-less scopes
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At least two list calls and up to 20 pages for a full scan; pages remaining after invalidation are wasted.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The list calls existed, but session rename did not invalidate their result.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Background startup discovery cannot complete usefully after rename, but these requests continue and keep the in-flight scan occupied.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch full task details for each sandbox task
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per uncached/changed sandbox task, bounded at concurrency 5; queued calls after invalidation are wasted.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These fetches could complete and populate the cache; rename did not make their entire pass uncommittable.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The scan remains in flight until every queued fetch settles, then returns failed because the generation changed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: PATCH the renamed task and invalidate the active discovery generation
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One PATCH creates the invalidation trigger; remaining discovery boundary count scales with the task inventory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Offline rename was a no-op and connected rename used AHP only, so neither invalidated discovery.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Makes all remaining active-pass work non-committable without cancelling or short-circuiting it.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cold task inventory: two repository scopes, up to 10 pages of 100 summaries, then one getTask per uncached sandbox task; effective getTask concurrency is 5.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Page requests are serial within each scope. Per-task detail requests use a shared Limiter of 5, but all queued items remain eligible after rename invalidates the pass. Overlapping discovery calls are otherwise coalesced by _discoveryInFlight.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Contribution-level persisted inventory is warm enough to expose rename UI, while the API service's task cache is cold on startup. Rename marks its task needsRefresh, but the active pass cannot commit any cache results because its generation is stale; a later pass must fetch again.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: generation capture/check placement, limits, limiter concurrency, restored-row timing, and invalidation are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of users with many sandbox tasks and exact request latency are unknown; persisted-row/startup overlap is directly supported by the restoration flow and the added in-flight test.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable boundary fan-out: the diff adds a realistic invalidation trigger while leaving all remaining network work running even though its result must be discarded.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all 11 changed files and traced offline/default-chat rename, connected rename, inventory persistence, task-cache refresh, and startup/incremental discovery. Submitted one medium-confidence-severity (high mechanism confidence) network boundary-fanout finding for uncancelled discovery after rename invalidation; no regression-fix learning signal applies.
